body: Valeant Pharmaceuticals, run by ex-McKinsey Michael Pearson, bought drug companies, slashed R&D (to ~3% of sales) and raised prices (e.g., Syprine +3,000%). It became a hedge-fund darling (Pershing Square, Sequoia Fund) and peaked at ~$262 in Aug 2015 with ~$30 bn of acquisition debt. Oct 2015: Citron Research alleged Valeant used undisclosed specialty pharmacy Philidor (which it had an option to buy for $100 m, first revealed on a call) and a 'network of clones' to push sales; Valeant cut ties on 30 Oct. The stock fell >90% by 2016-17 (single digits), Pearson left, Ackman exited with a ~$4 bn loss; renamed Bausch Health. Visible flags: (1) growth entirely acquired; organic volume weak; (2) heavy reliance on non-GAAP 'cash EPS' excluding acquisition costs that recurred every year; (3) debt/EBITDA ~5-7x; (4) tax inversion structure; (5) price increases (not volume) driving revenue, inviting political backlash (Sep 2015 Clinton tweet); (6) undisclosed related distribution channel (VIE) -> receivables/channel stuffing risk. Lesson: serial acquirers that adjust away recurring costs, lever up and grow only via price are fragile; star-investor ownership is not diligence.

data.early_signals: acquired growth; non-GAAP cash EPS; 5-7x leverage; price-not-volume; undisclosed Philidor
data.spotted_by: Citron Research (Andrew Left); short sellers; some pharma analysts

title: Valeant (2015-2017): roll-up, price hikes and Philidor
